subject.title: fix: Windows /restart falls back to in-process restart without changing PID

question: Should OpenClaw treat an installed default Windows Scheduled Task as the trusted restart supervisor even when the running gateway lacks the injected service marker environment variables?
rationale: Gateway restart fallback is compatibility- and availability-sensitive, and current code intentionally disables unmanaged detached Windows respawn to avoid orphaned children.

options.title: Accept schtasks probing
options.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95095 for a narrow probe that keeps unsafe unmanaged detached respawn disabled while recognizing an installed Scheduled Task.

options.title: Keep env-only detection
options.body: Reject the probe path and keep this behavior explicit, leaving manually-started Windows gateways to use the documented Scheduled Task run workaround.

options.title: Fold into broader Windows restart work
options.body: Defer this fix into the wider Windows restart reliability cluster if maintainers want one design to cover stderr surfacing, status truth, and SIGUSR1 handling together.

recommendation.title: Accept schtasks probing
recommendation.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95095 for a narrow probe that keeps unsafe unmanaged detached respawn disabled while recognizing an installed Scheduled Task.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the Windows Scheduled Task restart support and are also present in recent current-main history for the central restart files.
